subject: Stability incident: RCA summary, timeline, and customer verification checklist
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@clearstream.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com
Cc: Samira Patel <samira.patel@clearstream.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Service disruption on 2028-04-03 — observed latency and tokenization failures

Hi Rachel,

We saw a spike in tokenization latency and a handful of 500s across our primary inference routes starting ~14:45 PDT today. Impact: 3% of requests returned timeouts in our production lane, with a visible increase in request queuing for user-facing flows. This affected a subset of sessions for ~18 minutes.

Can you share a brief timeline and root cause as soon as you have it? Our SRE team is asking for the RCA and any mitigation steps you took. Also let us know if you expect any secondary effects (e.g., cache invalidation, replay needs).

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform — Clearstream Financial
alex.johnson@clearstream.com
+1 415-555-0132

(Attachment: screenshot-14-50.png [image/png])

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@clearstream.com>
Cc: Samira Patel <samira.patel@clearstream.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 15:39:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service disruption on 2028-04-03 — observed latency and tokenization failures

Hi Alex — thank you for the heads up and for the screenshot. We saw the same signal on our side and have a cross-functional incident team looking into it now (runtime, inference team, SRE).

Early details:
- We observed a KV-cache eviction storm tied to concurrent long-tail requests which increased kernel-switching overhead on a small fraction of hosts.
- Total customer-impact window on our telemetry matches your 14:45–15:03 PDT window.

Immediate mitigations already applied:
- Temporarily increased batching thresholds on the affected service group to reduce dispatch churn.
- Forced a controlled cache warm-up on impacted nodes to restore prefix-KV hit rates.

I will share a concise RCA and an action list within 24 hours and attach the timeline and action register for your review. Apologies for the disruption — we know you rely on steady inference latency.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
(Attachment: incident-acknowledgement.txt)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Service disruption on 2028-04-03 — draft RCA + timeline for Clearstream (please review)

Team — forwarding the customer note. Draft RCA and timeline are attached (rka_timeline.pdf) plus an action register (postmortem-action-register.csv). Request: please review and confirm wording for the "root cause" and the owner/ETA columns below before I send to Alex/Samira tomorrow morning.

Draft highlights (please edit inline):
- Root cause (draft): a workload-induced KV-cache eviction cascade combined with a pathological set of long-context requests that triggered additional attention to kernel scheduling on a subset of 12 GPUs in our us-west-2 pool.
- Contributing factors: default batching thresholds, an LRU threshold regression in last week's runtime rollout, and a probe that temporarily increased concurrent prefix loads for several tenants.
- Short-term remediation already executed: adjusted batching thresholds + forced cache warm-up.
- Medium-term actions (owners/ETA): runtime rollback and patch (Markus, 2028-04-06), automated eviction-detection alert (Neha, 2028-04-10), service-level canary for batching change (Marissa, 2028-04-08).

Please reply-all with any edits. I plan to send a customer-facing RCA and verification checklist at 9:00 PDT tomorrow.

Thanks — Rachel
(Attachments: rka_timeline.pdf, postmortem-action-register.csv)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@clearstream.com>
Cc: Samira Patel <samira.patel@clearstream.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Apr 2028 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service disruption on 2028-04-03 — RCA, timeline, and verification checklist

Alex / Samira — thanks for your patience. Attached is our customer-facing RCA summary and the verification checklist we propose to confirm service normalcy in your environment. Key points below; full timeline and the action register are attached (rka_timeline.pdf, postmortem-action-register.csv) and linked here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4dRCA-draft

Executive summary (concise):
- What happened: On 2028-04-03 14:45 PDT, an unusual concentration of long-context inference requests caused frequent KV-cache evictions on a small subset of nodes. Those evictions increased per-request kernel-switch overhead and caused transient queuing that produced timeouts for ~3% of requests.
- Immediate impact: 14:45–15:03 PDT; affected requests were routed to fallback nodes where possible; no data loss or model corruption observed.
- Root cause: a combination of an LRU threshold regression introduced in the runtime rollout on 2028-04-01 and a transient workload pattern (high-concurrency long-context requests) that exposed the regression on ~12 GPUs.

Mitigations completed during the incident:
- Adjusted batching thresholds to reduce dispatch churn (completed 14:52 PDT).
- Forced controlled cache warm-up on impacted hosts (completed 14:58 PDT).
- Applied temporary request-throttling to backstop further eviction storms (15:00 PDT).

Planned corrective actions (owners / target dates):
- Runtime patch to correct LRU threshold regression and harden eviction controls — Markus Klein — target 2028-04-06.
- Canary rollout with induced load tests (Marissa Cole) — target 2028-04-08.
- Auto-detect alert for eviction anomalies and automated rollback trigger (Neha Kapoor) — target 2028-04-10.
- Post-deploy verification runbook and customer test plan (Rachel Kim) — target 2028-04-07.

Customer verification checklist (please confirm):
1) Run the attached test script against your staging lane and confirm 99th percentile latency < 200ms for the tokenization step.
2) Confirm end-to-end user flows for your three highest-volume flows during a 30-minute window.
3) Reply to this thread with the test results; if you prefer, we can run a joint verification session on 2028-04-06 at 10:00 PDT.

Attachments: rka_timeline.pdf (detailed timeline + traces), postmortem-action-register.csv (action owner matrix).

If the checklist looks good I will mark action items as "in progress" in the register and follow up with a short note when the runtime patch is deployed.

Apologies again for the disruption — we appreciate the quick detection and the teamwork.

Best regards,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198
